Transparence.metaDesc: Information about the artificial intelligence systems used by CompliAI, in accordance with Article 50 of the AI Regulation (EU 2024/1689).
Transparence.title: Transparency — Artificial Intelligence
Transparence.intro: In accordance with Article 50(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on artificial intelligence (the "AI Act"), applicable since 2 August 2025, CompliAI informs you that you are interacting with an artificial intelligence system.
Transparence.s1aModel: Model: Claude Sonnet 4.6, developed by Anthropic PBC (San Francisco, USA).
Transparence.s1aUsage: Use: Answers to legal questions on the GDPR, the AI Act and European digital law. Generation of compliance documents (DPIA, FRIA, ROPA, etc.).
Transparence.s1aCorpus: Corpus: 14,000+ legal chunks from official texts (Official Journal of the EU, EDPB, CJEU, EU-27 national data protection authorities).
Transparence.s1bModel: Model: text-embedding-3-small, developed by OpenAI (San Francisco, USA).
Transparence.s1bUsage: Use: Vector search across the legal corpus to retrieve the relevant sources for each question.
Transparence.s2p1: The answers provided by CompliAI's AI consultant constitute legal decision support generated automatically from official European sources. They do not constitute professional legal advice within the meaning of regulations on regulated professions and must be validated by a professional before final application.
Transparence.s2p2: They do not replace consultation with a lawyer, a qualified legal expert or a data protection officer (DPO) for any decision with legal or financial consequences.
Transparence.s3li1: The model may produce inaccurate, incomplete or outdated information — always check the primary sources before use.
Transparence.s3li2: The corpus mainly covers EU law and the 27 Member States. National laws outside the EU are not covered.
Transparence.s3li3: Delegated acts, implementing acts and guidelines published after the indexing date may not be reflected.
Transparence.s3li4: The model does not remember conversations from one session to another (except via the Brain feature, which stores information explicitly saved by the user).
Transparence.s4li1: All indexed legal sources come from verified official publications (EU Official Journal, official websites of data protection authorities).
Transparence.s4li2: Each document added to the corpus is validated manually by the CompliAI team before becoming accessible to the assistant.
Transparence.s4li3: Quality test suite (golden set): 16 representative questions validated by our legal experts and tested after each corpus update.
Transparence.s4li4: Sourced citations: each answer cites the exact articles and provides links to official sources, allowing the user to verify every statement in the original legal text.
Transparence.s5intro: Questions asked to the AI assistant are transmitted to the following providers as part of the processing:
Transparence.s5li1: Anthropic PBC (USA) — processing of questions to generate answers. Transfer governed by the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). Default retention policy: up to 30 days for security and abuse prevention purposes. Data is not used to train Anthropic's models.
Transparence.s5li2: OpenAI, Inc. (USA) — semantic vectorisation of questions for corpus search. Transfer governed by the SCCs. Default retention policy: up to 30 days for abuse monitoring purposes. Data is not used to train OpenAI's models.
Transparence.s5outro: For more information on the processing of your personal data, see our <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.
Transparence.s6p1: Classification under assessment. A priori, CompliAI falls into the category of limited-risk AI systems within the meaning of Article 50 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, subject to transparency obligations towards end users. This page implements that obligation.
Transparence.s6p2: An in-depth assessment of the classification is planned with external legal counsel, in particular to check the applicability of Annex III (systems used in the administration of justice and democratic processes). In the meantime, CompliAI applies the transparency obligations of Article 50 as a precaution.
Transparence.s6contact: Contact for any question regarding this statement: <mail>privacy@compliai.eu</mail>
